cases.input:
name: Access of Sudoers File Content
id: 0f79c4d2-4e1f-4683-9c36-b5469a665e06
version: 1
schema_version: "1.0"
date: "2025-06-04"
author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
source:
  format: sigma
  repository: SigmaHQ/sigma
  rule_id: 0f79c4d2-4e1f-4683-9c36-b5469a665e06
  commit: release-20260810
  license: DRL-1.1
converted_by: Moussa Amine — sigma2copilot v0.1.0
status: experimental
type: TTP

description: >
  Detects the execution of a text-based file access or inspection utilities to
  read the content of /etc/sudoers in order to potentially list all users that
  have sudo rights. MITRE ATT&CK: T1592.004.

data_source:
  - Tetragon process_exec via Wazuh agent

search:
  index_pattern: "${INDEX_PATTERN}"
  size: 100
  sort:
    - timestamp: desc
  query:
    bool:
      must:
        - term:
            agent_name: "${AGENT_NAME}"
        - term:
            agent_labels_customer: "${CUSTOMER_CODE}"
        
        - bool:
            should:
              - wildcard:
                  data_process_exec_process_binary:
                    value: "*/cat"
                    case_insensitive: true
              - wildcard:
                  data_process_exec_process_binary:
                    value: "*/ed"
                    case_insensitive: true
              - wildcard:
                  data_process_exec_process_binary:
                    value: "*/egrep"
                    case_insensitive: true
              - wildcard:
                  data_process_exec_process_binary:
                    value: "*/emacs"
                    case_insensitive: true
              - wildcard:
                  data_process_exec_process_binary:
                    value: "*/fgrep"
                    case_insensitive: true
              - wildcard:
                  data_process_exec_process_binary:
                    value: "*/grep"
                    case_insensitive: true
              - wildcard:
                  data_process_exec_process_binary:
                    value: "*/head"
                    case_insensitive: true
              - wildcard:
                  data_process_exec_process_binary:
                    value: "*/less"
                    case_insensitive: true
              - wildcard:
                  data_process_exec_process_binary:
                    value: "*/more"
                    case_insensitive: true
              - wildcard:
                  data_process_exec_process_binary:
                    value: "*/nano"
                    case_insensitive: true
              - wildcard:
                  data_process_exec_process_binary:
                    value: "*/tail"
                    case_insensitive: true
            minimum_should_match: 1
        - wildcard:
            data_process_exec_process_arguments:
              value: "* /etc/sudoers*"
              case_insensitive: true
        # ---- end generated ----
        - range:
            timestamp:
              gte: "${START_TIME}"
              lte: "${END_TIME}"
  _source:
    - timestamp
    - agent_name
    - data_process_exec_process_binary
    - data_process_exec_process_arguments
    - data_process_exec_parent_binary
    - data_process_exec_process_uid

parameters:
  AGENT_NAME:
    description: "Target agent/host name"
    type: string
    required: true
    example: "DESKTOP-AM0HLGE"
  CUSTOMER_CODE:
    description: "Customer label for filtering"
    type: string
    required: true
    example: "lab"
  INDEX_PATTERN:
    description: "Elasticsearch index pattern"
    type: string
    required: true
    example: "wazuh-lab_*"
  START_TIME:
    description: "Query start time (ISO 8601 or relative)"
    type: datetime
    required: false
    default: "now-24h"
    example: "2026-04-08 00:00:00.000"
  END_TIME:
    description: "Query end time (ISO 8601 or relative)"
    type: datetime
    required: false
    default: "now"
    example: "2026-04-08 23:59:59.999"

how_to_implement: >
  Requires Tetragon deployed on the Linux endpoint emitting process_exec events
  (rule_groups "tetragon, process_exec"), shipped by the Wazuh agent and
  ingested into the wazuh-* indices. Tetragon records the executable in
  data_process_exec_process_binary and its arguments separately in
  data_process_exec_process_arguments. The detection looks for events where
  data_process_exec_process_binary matches '*/cat';
  data_process_exec_process_binary matches '*/ed';
  data_process_exec_process_binary matches '*/egrep', among other conditions.

known_false_positives: >
  Legitimate administration activities. Baseline expected activity in your
  environment and tune this detection before relying on it for automated
  response.

references:
  - https://github.com/sleventyeleven/linuxprivchecker/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1592/004/

response:
  message: >
    Access of Sudoers File Content detected on host $agent_name$. Matched
    data_process_exec_process_binary: $data_process_exec_process_binary$.
    Matched data_process_exec_process_arguments:
    $data_process_exec_process_arguments$. MITRE ATT&CK: T1592.004
  risk_score: 50
  severity: medium
  risk_objects:
    - field: agent_name
      type: system
      score: 50
  threat_objects:
    - field: data_process_exec_process_binary
      type: other
    - field: data_process_exec_process_arguments
      type: other

tags:
  asset_type: Endpoint
  mitre_attack_id:
    - T1592.004
  custom_tags:
    - sudoers
    - content
    - linux
    - tetragon
    - process_creation
    - reconnaissance
  product:
    - Wazuh
  security_domain: endpoint

graylog:
  query: (data_process_exec_process_binary:/.*\/[Cc][Aa][Tt]/ OR data_process_exec_process_binary:/.*\/[Ee][Dd]/ OR data_process_exec_process_binary:/.*\/[Ee][Gg][Rr][Ee][Pp]/ OR data_process_exec_process_binary:/.*\/[Ee][Mm][Aa][Cc][Ss]/ OR data_process_exec_process_binary:/.*\/[Ff][Gg][Rr][Ee][Pp]/ OR data_process_exec_process_binary:/.*\/[Gg][Rr][Ee][Pp]/ OR data_process_exec_process_binary:/.*\/[Hh][Ee][Aa][Dd]/ OR data_process_exec_process_binary:/.*\/[Ll][Ee][Ss][Ss]/ OR data_process_exec_process_binary:/.*\/[Mm][Oo][Rr][Ee]/ OR data_process_exec_process_binary:/.*\/[Nn][Aa][Nn][Oo]/ OR data_process_exec_process_binary:/.*\/[Tt][Aa][Ii][Ll]/) AND data_process_exec_process_arguments:/.* \/[Ee][Tt][Cc]\/[Ss][Uu][Dd][Oo][Ee][Rr][Ss].*/

version: 1

author: Austin Songer @austinsonger
source:

  risk_score: 50

cases.label: rule file detections/web/exploit_public_facing_application_via_apache_commons_text.yaml
cases.input:
name: Exploit Public Facing Application via Apache Commons Text
id: 19a481e0-c97c-4d14-b1db-75a708eb592e
version: 1
schema_version: "1.0"
date: "2026-05-12"
author: SOCFortress LLC
status: production
type: Anomaly

description: >
  This analytic detects attempts to exploit CVE-2022-42889 (Text4Shell),
  a critical Remote Code Execution vulnerability in the Apache Commons
  Text library affecting versions 1.5 through 1.9. The vulnerability
  exists in the StringSubstitutor interpolator class, where untrusted
  user input passed to lookup functions can result in arbitrary code
  execution, DNS lookups, or remote URL fetches via the script, url,
  and dns lookup keys. The detection inspects Nginx web access logs
  (web-accesslog decoder) for HTTP GET or POST requests where the URI
  query string contains hallmark Text4Shell payload patterns. The query
  uses a two-stage logic equivalent to the original Splunk scoring
  approach: it requires at least one HIGH-confidence indicator
  (presence of the utf-8:http/, url, dns, or script lookup keys, which
  are the canonical Text4Shell exploit vectors) AND at least one
  additional indicator from either the high-confidence list or the
  supporting list (env, file, getRuntime, java, localhost, properties,
  resource, sys, xml, base). This combination produces the same
  effective threshold as the published Splunk rule's score >= 3 logic.
  This is a known T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application),
  T1133 (External Remote Services), and T1505.003 (Web Shell)
  technique. If confirmed malicious, successful exploitation could
  allow attackers to execute arbitrary code on the vulnerable web
  server, leading to full system compromise, credential theft, data
  exfiltration, web shell installation, or lateral movement into the
  internal network.

data_source:
  - Nginx Access

search:
  index_pattern: "${INDEX_PATTERN}"
  size: 100
  sort:
    - timestamp: desc
  query:
    bool:
      must:
        - term:
            agent_labels_customer: "${CUSTOMER_CODE}"
        - term:
            decoder_name: "web-accesslog"
        - bool:
            should:
              - term:
                  data_protocol: "GET"
              - term:
                  data_protocol: "POST"
            minimum_should_match: 1
        - bool:
            should:
              - wildcard:
                  data_url:
                    value: "*:utf-8:http*"
                    case_insensitive: true
              - wildcard:
                  data_url:
                    value: "*url*"
                    case_insensitive: true
              - wildcard:
                  data_url:
                    value: "*dns*"
                    case_insensitive: true
              - wildcard:
                  data_url:
                    value: "*script*"
                    case_insensitive: true
            minimum_should_match: 1
        - bool:
            should:
              - wildcard:
                  data_url:
                    value: "*:utf-8:http*"
                    case_insensitive: true
              - wildcard:
                  data_url:
                    value: "*env*"
                    case_insensitive: true
              - wildcard:
                  data_url:
                    value: "*file*"
                    case_insensitive: true
              - wildcard:
                  data_url:
                    value: "*getRuntime*"
                    case_insensitive: true
              - wildcard:
                  data_url:
                    value: "*java*"
                    case_insensitive: true
              - wildcard:
                  data_url:
                    value: "*localhost*"
                    case_insensitive: true
              - wildcard:
                  data_url:
                    value: "*properties*"
                    case_insensitive: true
              - wildcard:
                  data_url:
                    value: "*resource*"
                    case_insensitive: true
              - wildcard:
                  data_url:
                    value: "*sys*"
                    case_insensitive: true
              - wildcard:
                  data_url:
                    value: "*xml*"
                    case_insensitive: true
              - wildcard:
                  data_url:
                    value: "*base*"
                    case_insensitive: true
              - wildcard:
                  data_url:
                    value: "*url*"
                    case_insensitive: true
              - wildcard:
                  data_url:
                    value: "*dns*"
                    case_insensitive: true
              - wildcard:
                  data_url:
                    value: "*script*"
                    case_insensitive: true
            minimum_should_match: 1
        - range:
            timestamp:
              gte: "${START_TIME}"
              lte: "${END_TIME}"
  _source:
    - timestamp
    - agent_name
    - agent_ip
    - data_protocol
    - data_url
    - data_srcip
    - data_id
    - full_log
    - location
    - rule_id
    - rule_description
    - rule_groups

parameters:
  AGENT_NAME:
    description: "Target agent/host name (web server)"
    type: string
    required: false
    example: "socfortress-lab-agent"
  CUSTOMER_CODE:
    description: "Customer label for filtering"
    type: string
    required: true
    example: "lab"
  INDEX_PATTERN:
    description: "Elasticsearch index pattern"
    type: string
    required: true
    example: "wazuh-lab_*"
  START_TIME:
    description: "Query start time (ISO 8601 or relative)"
    type: datetime
    required: false
    default: "now-24h"
    example: "2026-05-12 00:00:00.000"
  END_TIME:
    description: "Query end time (ISO 8601 or relative)"
    type: datetime
    required: false
    default: "now"
    example: "2026-05-12 23:59:59.999"

how_to_implement: >
  This detection requires Nginx access logs to be collected by a Wazuh
  agent and parsed by the web-accesslog decoder, then forwarded to the
  Wazuh Indexer. Ensure the Wazuh agent is configured to monitor the
  Nginx access log file (typically /var/log/nginx/access.log) and that
  the standard SOCFortress decoder set is in use so the data_protocol,
  data_url, data_srcip, and data_id fields are populated. The detection
  is intentionally broad in the supporting-indicator clause to mirror
  the original Splunk scoring approach. For higher-fidelity alerting in
  noisy environments, the supporting-indicator list can be tuned by
  removing the most common keywords (sys, base, xml) that may appear
  in legitimate API traffic. Alternatively, raise the rule to TTP-level
  fidelity by requiring at least two matches from the high-confidence
  list (utf-8:http, url, dns, script) - this approximates the Splunk
  rule's recommended escalation path. Pair this network detection with
  endpoint monitoring of the target web server for follow-on process
  execution (java spawning shell processes, outbound connections from
  the JVM process) for full-coverage detection.

known_false_positives: >
  False positives are possible when legitimate application traffic
  contains substrings matching the supporting-indicator keywords
  (env, file, java, localhost, properties, resource, sys, xml, base,
  url, dns, script). These are common substrings that may appear in
  legitimate REST API paths, query parameters, or framework-specific
  URLs. The high-confidence indicator requirement (utf-8:http, url,
  dns, or script lookup keys) significantly reduces false positives,
  but tuning may still be required - allow-list specific URI paths
  or source IP ranges as needed for known legitimate traffic
  patterns. The original Splunk rule notes that raising to TTP and
  requiring two HIGH-confidence matches can eliminate most false
  positives.

references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1133/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1505/003/
  - https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2022-42889
  - https://sysdig.com/blog/cve-2022-42889-text4shell/
  - https://lists.apache.org/thread/n2bd4vdsgkqh2tm14l1wyc3jyol7s1om
  - https://www.rapid7.com/blog/post/2022/10/17/cve-2022-42889-keep-calm-and-stop-saying-4shell/
  - https://github.com/kljunowsky/CVE-2022-42889-text4shell

response:
  message: >
    A URL containing Apache Commons Text (Text4Shell, CVE-2022-42889)
    exploit indicators was requested against web server $agent_name$
    by source IP $data_srcip$. HTTP method: $data_protocol$.
    Requested URL: $data_url$. HTTP response status: $data_id$.
    Raw log: $full_log$. This pattern is consistent with attempts to
    exploit the StringSubstitutor lookup vulnerability in Apache
